record_identity.title: AI delegation reframed as transfer of authority, responsibility and accountability

summary: Google DeepMind researchers propose an adaptive framework for intelligent AI delegation in which task allocation is not treated as mere decomposition. The framework expressly incorporates transfer of authority, responsibility and accountability; clear roles and boundaries; clarity of intent; and mechanisms for establishing trust between human and AI delegators and delegatees in complex delegation networks.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: The paper is a material external research signal that multi-agent delegation is being framed as a governance and authority-transfer problem rather than only an orchestration problem. That distinction is directly relevant to existing VIGIL concerns about constraint drift, delegated execution, policy laundering and cross-organisational authority, while remaining broader than any one current failure mode.

source_records.author_or_publisher: Nenad Tomašev, Matija Franklin and Simon Osindero — Google DeepMind
source_records.deployment_context: Complex delegation networks involving human and AI delegators and delegatees.
source_records.source_context: The paper proposes intelligent AI delegation as a sequence of decisions involving task allocation while also incorporating transfer of authority, responsibility and accountability; clear specifications of roles and boundaries; clarity of intent; and mechanisms for establishing trust. The abstract states that the framework applies to both human and AI delegators and delegatees and is intended to inform protocols for an emerging agentic web.
source_records.relevance_note: Primary research signal that delegation governance must preserve authority, responsibility, accountability, roles, boundaries, intent and trust rather than treating delegation as task decomposition alone.

migration_notes: This is a bounded observation of a single external research source, not a VIGIL RESEARCH synthesis.
Delegation itself is not classified as a failure. The observation preserves the paper's distinction between task decomposition and governed transfer of authority, responsibility and accountability.
next_action: Monitor follow-on work, protocol development and empirical delegation failures. Use this record as contextual evidence when reviewing delegated-authority, reauthorisation, provenance and accountability questions; do not convert coordination or delegation itself into a failure mode.
